name: NGC 4858 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 4858, a jellyfish galaxy in the Coma Cluster, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc4858-hubble
story: As NGC 4858 moves through the Coma Cluster, a fierce headwind called ram pressure is stripping gas from its disk. The pressure bends its spiral arms into shapes that look like bunny ears and drags its gas into a jellyfish-like tail.

claims.text: NGC 4858 is a jellyfish galaxy in the Coma Cluster undergoing ram pressure stripping, studied with Hubble F350LP/F600LP images
NGC 4858 was a target of HST program 13777 on ram pressure stripping of bright spiral galaxies in Coma
Ram pressure, a 'wind', strips gas from the galaxy and gives it a jellyfish look; distorted spiral arm features look like bunny ears
